key_insight: Crosswind kite wakes modestly reduce lift, but rotor-slipstream treatment near the wing can reverse the predicted rotor effect.
engineering_relevance: Reliable airborne wind energy load and farm-power predictions require careful wake sizing, vortex-core selection, and rotor–wing interaction modeling.
method: Vortex step aerodynamics coupled to a time-marching free vortex wake in OpenFAWE.
Lumped-mass tether and actuator-disc rotors represented by shed vortex rings.
Single- and multi-kite simulations assessing wake resolution and rotor-slipstream treatments.
evidence_signal: Validation showed lift agreement within 3.1% of RANS for the TU Delft V3 kite; a second unit one loop diameter downstream lost 0.5% lift and 2.2% aerodynamic power.
watch_item: Free rotor-ring simulations did not converge with time-step refinement, and alternative slipstream treatments shifted the predicted lift effect from +1.9% to −3.5%.
paper_title: Free-vortex-wake dynamics of airborne wind energy kites in crosswind flight
